headline: No documented interaction path; both agents are docs-only, runnable=false, and expose no shared I/O surfaces or egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. Agent A has no I/O surfaces and network_egress is none; agent B likewise has no I/O surfaces and network_egress is none. With no shared channel, B cannot ingest A's outputs by default.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared copy-paste channels.
Do not mount a common workspace or clipboard bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data-leakage pathway is evident from the profiles. Both agents are docs-only, runnable=false, touch no data classes, and have network_egress set to none, so neither can exfiltrate the other's context through a documented default path.
conditions: IF either agent is deployed with a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any shared directory.
Keep both agents non-runnable unless a sandbox is defined.
requires-engineering: define explicit data-handling and retention controls before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability conflict is not supported by the profiles. Neither agent requests permissions, neither has write surfaces, and both have network_egress none, so there is no documented overlapping mutable resource to contend over.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or mutable service, conflict risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access.
Keep mutable resources outside the pair's scope.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway is not documented. Agent A is an awesome-list repository and agent B is a memory system, but both profiles show runnable=false and no I/O surfaces, so B cannot automatically treat A's output as authoritative in a default deployment.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding A-generated text into B without verification, cascading error becomes plausible.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before any downstream use.
Do not auto-ingest A's outputs into B.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for any future pipeline between them.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. The profiles do not declare data classes touched, residency, retention, or regulated-data handling for either agent, so there is no documented basis for a residency or retention breach between A and B.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes or residency constraints, compliance risk must be reassessed.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy checks if regulated data is introduced.
